A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaIRMaker. The complete main texts and appendices, including algorithms, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original bias-mitigation, utility, runtime, DPO-combination and ablation experiments across multiple LLMs in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds knowledge and reasoning evaluations, baseline comparisons, an auto-search ablation and further interpretability analyses.

M1.justification: The search objective, Algorithm 1, filtering, refinement objectives, refiner model and inference pipeline are unchanged. Random Fairwords selection was already documented in v1's limitations. The newly disclosed LoRA settings do not establish a change to the method.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated general-knowledge coverage through MMLU and commonsense completion through HellaSwag (Table 4), substantially broadening utility testing beyond open-ended instruction following. GenderAlign, BBQ-gender, Dolly Eval, Instruct Eval and BPO Eval remain.

E2.justification: MBIAS becomes an evaluated post-processing comparator on GA-test in v2 Tables 3 and 9; v1 cited it without reporting this comparison. CF-D, Desc-D and Intervention remain, as does the main DPO comparison.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation judge set changes from GPT-4 and Llama3.1 to GPT-4, DeepSeek-V3 and Gemini-2.0-Flash, affecting the central response evaluations. V2 also introduces accuracy-based MMLU and HellaSwag testing. Evaluation prompts and retained dataset sample counts are unchanged, although Appendix F.2 still lists the old judges.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of auto-search necessity alongside the existing filtering and refinement ablations (Table 6), extends emotion analysis to Llama2-Alpaca, and adds a with/without-Fairwords case study (Appendix D.5). The supplementary Llama3.1 evaluation of DPO combinations is removed; the GPT-4 analysis remains.

E5.justification: V2 newly states that all results are averaged over four random seeds. V1 mentions replication without specifying a count. This adds reporting information without establishing an increase in runs; confidence intervals and dispersion estimates are still absent.

E6.justification: V2 adds benchmark, MBIAS, judge and analysis results, and revises existing values. Llama2-Alpaca's FaIRMaker BBQ scores change from 0.518/0.376 to 0.224/0.157 (Table 2), while its GPT-4 win rate changes from 55.61% to 53.15% (Figure 3). Figure 5's timing observations also change. Existing GPT-4 response-score results are retained in appendix Tables 9 and 10; scores from different judges are not direct performance gains.

T1.justification: The optimization losses, first-order approximation and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. V2 spells out the already-used BBQ metrics as explanatory detail; it does not identify a revised metric or introduce new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an automated, model-independent auto-search-and-refinement framework that mitigates gender bias while preserving utility across open- and closed-source models. V2's expanded abstract restates contributions already present in v1's introduction; the conclusion retains their scope.

C2.justification: V2 removes explicit limitations concerning training-data diversity and evaluator bias, while adding arguments for straightforward adaptation to other biases and acceptable scalability overhead. It also expands interpretations concerning reasoning generalization, MBIAS limitations and Fairwords as emotional seed signals that guide refinement.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies the previously undocumented refiner training recipe: LoRA rank 8, scaling 16, dropout 0.05, AdamW at 1e-5, cosine scheduling, ten epochs, four-step gradient accumulation and FP16. V1 identifies the model and objective but omits these implementation details. Existing search settings and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for MMLU, HellaSwag, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini and DPO, and explicitly positions FaIRMaker against MBIAS post-processing. The related-work taxonomy and broader novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 revises and expands the abstract and introductory explanations, edits terminology and affiliation information, and reorganizes appendices to separate configuration and limitations. Most method prose, related work and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Examples and word clouds are rearranged, Figure 3 becomes a three-judge display, the timing plot is redrawn, ablation and interpretation tables gain columns, and new benchmark and case-study tables appear. Several retained result tables move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added accuracy benchmarks, direct auto-search ablation and refiner training recipe address gaps in v1's validation and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removed evaluator-bias caveats and insufficient qualification of new findings: Figure 3 shows Gemini's GPT-3.5 win rate below its loss rate despite the universal improvement statement, and Table 6 shows better BBQ scores without auto-search.
